summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: SemiAnalysis is the founder-owned research firm whose ClusterMAX rating decides, for the 31 other dossiers in this corpus that cite it, which GPU clouds count as Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze or 'Not Recommended' — and it is simultaneously a newsletter (318,000-plus subscribers at USD 70 a month or USD 690 a year), a vendor of sixteen institutional data models sold on request to 'hyperscalers, neoclouds, many of the world's largest hedge funds, and government agencies', a consultancy that performs paid technical assessments with the same toolkit it rates with, and, since July 2026, a venture investor filing for a USD 400 million fund — so its independence is a claim the firm makes about itself, backed by a compensation disclaimer printed once (ClusterMAX 1.0, March 2025) and not repeated in 2.0 or 3.0, and tested by a live employment suit alleging that material non-public information from a Fluidstack investment vehicle the founder led was to be put into paid research (an allegation SemiAnalysis denies). BACKGROUND. Founded 22 May 2020 by Dylan Patel as a WordPress blog, moved to Substack in 2021; merged with Doug O'Laughlin's Fabricated Knowledge (November 2024), absorbed Chips & Wafers (September 2025) and acquired Citrini Research (September 2026, price undisclosed). Legal entity SemiAnalysis LLC, a Florida limited liability company (court caption; Florida registry L22000096118; USPTO serial 99336949), with branch registrations in California, New York, Oregon and Utah. Revenue, per The Information (April 2026): about USD 20 million in 2025, projected to exceed USD 100 million in 2026; 'less than 5% of revenue comes from Substack' (Substrate, September 2026); the company publishes no accounts. Products: the newsletter; Core Research and the weekly Cache Up digest for institutional investors (reviewed by a Series 16 supervisory analyst); the Accelerator & HBM, Datacenter Industry (5,000-plus facilities), China Datacenter (1,000-plus facilities, launched 25 September 2026), AI Cloud TCO, AI Networking, Wafer Fab Equipment, Foundry, Memory, Energy, Industrials, Tokenomics, Space DC TCO and VR NVL72 models — every one 'a separate institutional offering, not part of the newsletter subscription' and priced on request except the VR NVL72 Model at USD 10,000; ClusterMAX (1.0 March 2025, 2.0 November 2025, 2.1 April 2026, 3.0 23 September 2026: 323 providers tracked, 77 reviewed, 19 medallions); InferenceX, the open-source (Apache 2.0) inference benchmark formerly InferenceMAX, launched October 2025 and renamed February 2026 with compute donated by rated providers; and consulting 'from retained advisory to one-off projects to hourly calls'. Collection gaps: audited revenue, the revenue split by product, the client list, whether any rated neocloud is a paying client, badge-licensing terms, and the fund's capital raised (Form D: USD 400 million target, USD 0 sold at filing; USD 500 million 'confirmed' only by a company-sourced profile).
ecosystemRole: The corpus's tenth `advisor` and the only one whose product is a rating the other dossiers rely on: ClusterMAX tiers appear in the neocloud dossiers (coreweave, nebius, crusoe, lambda, iren, fluidstack, nscale, firmus, whitefiber, g42, humain, alibaba-cloud), its 800 VDC and datacenter-power analysis in the power-conversion and SST dossiers (vertiv, delta-electronics, megmeet, liteon, vicor, infineon, amperesand, dg-matrix, heron-power, novos-power, piller, voltagrid), and its datacenter and China models in the hyperscaler and landlord dossiers (bytedance, alibaba-cloud, chindata, google, xai, amd, supermicro, coolit). What those dossiers rest on, stated plainly: a relative rating of managed GPU clusters, tested hands-on by SemiAnalysis staff on clusters the providers grant (so not mystery-shopped), scored on ten published criteria with a three-phase audit, performance and reliability protocol, informed by 'well over 200' user interviews, re-run on a 'roughly 6 months' cadence that has in practice been 7.5 and 10.5 months, with no compensation disclaimer since the first edition and no published policy on rated-company consulting, badge licensing or staff and fund holdings. The firm sells models and consulting to the hyperscalers and neoclouds it rates and benchmarks, its founder's investment vehicle sat in a neocloud (Fluidstack) that was rated Gold in 2.0, and the only public response to the conflict question is a relayed sentence that 'providers cannot purchase their ranking and client compensation is not tied to the ratings'. The seat is real — buyers from OpenAI's Stargate team to General Atlantic endorse it and tier moves move stock prices — and so is the gap. No segment of this corpus's value chain holds a market-intelligence vendor, so the company is recorded in the segments registry's unassigned list.

productsAndServices.name: ClusterMAX™ — the GPU cloud rating system
productsAndServices.category: Rating and technical assessment — managed GPU clusters
productsAndServices.description: A relative, five-tier rating (Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze, Underperforming; plus 'Not Recommended – Unavailable' and, from 3.0, a 'Participation Ribbon') of managed GPU cluster providers, produced by SemiAnalysis staff testing clusters the providers grant against ten published criteria — Security, Lifecycle, Orchestration, Storage, Networking, Reliability, Monitoring, Pricing, Partnerships, Availability — complemented by end-user interviews. Editions: 1.0 (26 March 2025; 26 providers rated, 169 tracked), 2.0 (6 November 2025; 84 rated, 209 tracked, 37 medallions), 2.1 (April 2026; site-only update, no full re-test), 3.0 (23 September 2026; 77 reviewed, 323 tracked, 19 medallions, 15 Participation Ribbons). The ratings site (clustermax.ai) is free; the full provider write-ups are paid newsletter posts; the Phase 1 audit tool is open source.
highlights: Method, 3.0 (company text): 'Phase 1: Audit — … yes/no questions. Is the cluster setup properly? … It takes about 15 minutes to run. It's available on GitHub or via uv pip install clustermax … We have released this part for free … The rest we keep internally'; 'Phase 2: Performance — puts a pass/fail threshold on the performance characteristics' via microbenchmarks and real-world training and inference runs; Phase 3 reliability — 'an 8-hour burn-in on the GPUs and network … destructive testing' with injected XIDs, reboots and PCIe resets; 'we always complement this testing by contacting customers of all these providers' — 'well over 200 end users'. Scope: 'we are ranking managed clusters … We are not testing who can build the best powered shell.'

What 'Unavailable' means (3.0): 'four types of companies: Those that we have previously tested who now claim to have zero spare capacity and/or refuse to test with us … Those that are yet to launch … Those who are big and important, but who we cannot test properly due to geographic or regulatory concerns … Those who are too small to be relevant' — Fluidstack, Nscale, HUMAIN, Alibaba Cloud and Scaleway sit in that bucket in 3.0, and the post accuses a group including Nscale of 'misleading investors (i.e., lying)' about offering managed clusters.

Cadence as stated against cadence as delivered: 1.0 promised re-evaluation 'every 3-6 months'; 2.0 said major versions 'every ~6 months' with minor versions in between; actual intervals were 7.5 months (1.0 → 2.0) and 10.5 months (2.0 → 3.0), with the 2.1 site update at 5.5 months. 3.0 names no cadence and announces inference-endpoint testing and a 'PostTrainingX' ranking for future versions.

Independence, in the company's own words: 1.0 opened 'The ClusterMAX™ Rating System and content within this article were prepared independently by SemiAnalysis. No part of SemiAnalysis's compensation by our clients was, is, or will be directly or indirectly related to the specific tiering, ratings or comments expressed.' Neither 2.0 nor 3.0 repeats that sentence; neither discloses rated-company consulting relationships, badge-licensing terms or staff and fund holdings. The clustermax.ai legal notice invites 'Licensing inquiries and partnership proposals' and reserves financial-product use of the ratings. Relayed response to a September 2026 'pay to rank' accusation (Yahoo Finance): 'providers cannot purchase their ranking and … client compensation is not tied to the ratings'.

The paid adjunct (3.0): 'include a SemiAnalysis Technical Assessment during acceptance testing and monthly SLA performance reviews. We perform this Technical Assessment using our cmax utility and a comprehensive, proprietary process. Please contact us at clustermax@semianalysis.com' — the rating toolkit sold as a service to cluster buyers; the careers page files ClusterMAX under 'Consulting & diligence'.

3.0 placements that this corpus's dossiers carry: Platinum CoreWeave and Nebius; Gold Oracle and Google Cloud (two members, not three); Silver Azure, Lambda, TensorWave, Firmus, GMI; Bronze Crusoe (from Gold), AWS, Together AI, DigitalOcean, Prime Intellect, Hyperstack; Participation Ribbon Core42, Vultr, Hyperbolic and twelve others; Underperforming IREN, WhiteFiber, Sharon AI; Unavailable Fluidstack, Nscale, HUMAIN, Alibaba Cloud, Scaleway, Cirrascale and the yet-to-launch list including 'SpaceXAI'. Market reaction (24/7 Wall St, 25 September 2026): IREN −4%, CoreWeave −3%, Nebius −2% in a week that also carried Redburn notes.
productsAndServices.positioning: SemiAnalysis calls it 'the industry standard'; buyers and investors quoted on clustermax.ai (OpenAI Stargate's Peter Hoeschele, Meta's Santosh Janardhan, Michael Dell, Atreides' Gavin Baker — 'the industry standard for evaluating GPU cloud providers' — Altimeter's Brad Gerstner, General Atlantic) endorse it, and no comparable third-party rating of managed GPU clouds exists; MLCommons' MLPerf benchmarks hardware, not clouds. Criticism on the record: Hot Aisle CEO Jon Stevens ('Influence as a Service', December 2025 — Hot Aisle is itself a Bronze-rated provider), the 'pay to rank' charge of September 2026, and remio.ai's note that SemiAnalysis 'communicates with companies during testing' rather than mystery-shopping.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Free tier list and badges at clustermax.ai; full reviews behind the paid newsletter (USD 70/month, USD 690/year); Phase 1 audit CLI free (GitHub, `uv pip install clustermax`); Technical Assessment and SLA reviews sold as consulting by email; badge use by rated providers (CoreWeave, Nebius, Together AI, TensorWave publish it) with no published licence terms.
targetSegments: The rated providers themselves (feedback and badges)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Inference-endpoint testing and a 'PostTrainingX' ranking announced for 'future versions'; no dated 4.0.

productsAndServices.name: InferenceX™ (formerly InferenceMAX) — open-source continuous inference benchmark
productsAndServices.category: Open-source benchmark — AI accelerators and serving stacks
productsAndServices.description: An Apache 2.0 benchmark that 'runs [a] suite of benchmarks every night on hundreds of chips' across NVIDIA (Vera Rubin NVL72, GB300 NVL72, GB200 NVL72, B300, B200, H200, H100), AMD (MI355X, MI325X, MI300X) and Google TPUv7x hardware and the SGLang, vLLM and TensorRT-LLM stacks, publishing a free live dashboard of fixed-sequence serving results and, since August 2026, AgentX — a 'long-context, multi-turn agentic coding workload'. Launched as InferenceMAX on 9 October 2025; renamed InferenceX with v2 on 16 February 2026; v3/AgentX on 24 August 2026.
highlights: Stated purpose: 'designed to be a neutral benchmark, not cherry-picked to promote any specific vendor'; 'our independent, vendor neutral, reproducible benchmark'; 'Our benchmark has been widely reproduced, validated and/or supported by almost every major buyer of compute.' GitHub ~1.8k stars; 'Only SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX repo contains the Official InferenceX™ result'.

Supporters quoted on the project site include Jensen Huang and Ian Buck (NVIDIA), Lisa Su and Anush Elangovan (AMD), Peter Hoeschele (OpenAI Stargate), Scott Guthrie (Microsoft), Jay Jackson (OCI), Tri Dao, Simon Mo (vLLM), and the CEOs or CTOs of CoreWeave, Nebius, TensorWave, Crusoe, Supermicro, Vultr, Lambda and Firmus — the rated neoclouds among them 'supply compute for InferenceMAX' (Nebius partner catalog; Crusoe blog: 'we're proud to support InferenceMAX'). No fee, sponsorship or paid-placement statement exists either way.

Findings this corpus's dossiers cite: v2 (February 2026) 'the first third party benchmark to test disagg+wideEP multi-node FP4 and FP8 MI355X performance', finding MI355X competitive on FP8 disaggregated perf-per-TCO and behind on FP4 (the amd dossier); 'Vera Rubin NVL72 Agentic Inference: 67x better Performance per Dollar' (September 2026); 'TPU Inference Externalization Full Steam Ahead' (September 2026).

Critique on the record (Silicon Data, March 2026): results come from 'hardware that SemiAnalysis operates internally' with 'no way for the public to run InferenceX on their own systems', hardware 'likely provided' by NVIDIA and AMD, and a repository that 'lacks structure'. AMD disputed a separate SemiAnalysis report (MI455X volume slipping to 2027) in February 2026 — 'BS. Right on target for H2 2026.'
productsAndServices.positioning: Against MLCommons' MLPerf (periodic, vendor-submitted) and vendor-run benchmarks: nightly, third-party-run, open code; against Silicon Data's SiliconMark, which positions itself as the customer-runnable alternative.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Free and open source (Apache 2.0); dashboard public at inferencex.com; the analysis posts are paid newsletter content; compute donated by supporters.
targetSegments: ML engineers and capacity planners at AI labs and neoclouds
productsAndServices.roadmap: CollectiveX and OperatorX (beta) and a power model listed in the repository; TPU and Trainium coverage expanding.

The structural fact for a reader of this corpus: the same owner now runs a rating system (ClusterMAX), a paid technical-assessment service built on it, institutional models sold to the rated providers' customers and competitors, and a venture fund that invests in the sector it rates. financials.commentary: SemiAnalysis is a founder-owned Florida LLC that files no accounts; every revenue and headcount figure above is a company statement relayed by a named outlet or a third-party count, dated to the piece that carried it, and where two outlets differ both are stated. The SEC record is the exception: the four Form D filings for the SemiAnalysis Capital vehicles are primary and were read from sec.gov. What a reader can rely on without caveat: the USD 70/month and USD 690/year newsletter prices, the 'contact sales' pricing of every model except the USD 10,000 VR NVL72 model, the USD 400m Fund I target with nil sold at filing, and the two fully subscribed USD 20m SPVs.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that ClusterMAX is the firm's distribution engine rather than its revenue line: it is free to read, cited by 31 other dossiers in this corpus, displayed as a badge by CoreWeave, Nebius, Together AI and TensorWave, and converts into paid work three ways the company itself describes — the 'SemiAnalysis Technical Assessment during acceptance testing and monthly SLA performance reviews' sold from the 3.0 post, the AI Cloud TCO Model 'trusted by the world's largest GPU buyers' plugged inside provider reviews, and consulting 'for the people deploying capital'. Basis: the careers page files ClusterMAX under 'Consulting & diligence'; Substrate and Asymmetrix put the newsletter under 5% of revenue; the 2025→2026 revenue path (~USD 20m → >USD 100m projected) coincides with the rating's second and third editions.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the independence record has weakened edition by edition, as a matter of what is printed: 1.0 (March 2025) opened with the compensation disclaimer ('No part of SemiAnalysis's compensation by our clients was, is, or will be directly or indirectly related to the specific tiering'); 2.0 and 3.0 carry no compensation, conflict or staff-investment disclosure, and 3.0 explains Fluidstack's fall to 'Unavailable' without mentioning the USD 50m Fluidstack SPV Patel led. The company's position, relayed by Yahoo Finance in September 2026, is that 'providers cannot purchase their ranking' and 'client compensation is not tied to the ratings'; no evidence of pay-for-rank has been produced by any critic. We note the loudest critic (Hot Aisle's CEO) runs a Bronze-rated provider.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the rated providers are, as a class, also counterparties: InferenceMAX/InferenceX runs on compute donated by Crusoe, CoreWeave, Nebius, TensorWave, Oracle and Together (Nebius's own partner catalogue says it 'supplies compute for InferenceMAX'); 'most providers granted us at least 4 B300 nodes' for 3.0 testing; the 3.0 text refers to 'clients of our industry-leading Datacenter Model' inside the Nebius section. Whether any rated provider pays SemiAnalysis for models, assessments or badge display is undisclosed by every party. The confidence is moderate because the dependency is documented and the payment is not.

4. **(High confidence)** We assess that the firm has become a market participant in the sector it rates. The SEC record is unambiguous: Fund I (USD 400m target), two fully sold USD 20m SPVs and a USD 19.8m third-party feeder since July 2026; a board seat at Positron AI; reported stakes in about 20 start-ups. The compliance page restricts personal trading in 'hundreds of securities' and bars securities ratings and target prices, but is silent on private-company holdings and on consulting for rated providers — the two exposures that actually exist. For a reader of this corpus the practical rule is: treat a ClusterMAX tier as a technically grounded assessment by a firm with undisclosed commercial and investment ties to several of the rated companies, not as an audit.

5. **(High confidence)** We assess that the 3.0 edition is materially harsher than 2.0 and that this is the edition the corpus should carry: Gold shrank to two (Oracle, Google); Nebius rose to Platinum; Crusoe fell from Gold to Bronze; Fluidstack, Nscale and HUMAIN went 'Unavailable'; IREN, WhiteFiber and Sharon AI were placed 'Underperforming'; Core42, Vultr and Hyperbolic received a 'Participation Ribbon'. The methodology shift — security as a gate after 'Most Neoclouds Suck At Security' (30 August 2026), auto-remediation and handover delays penalised, hands-on testing of granted B300 nodes — explains most of the movement. Four inbound dossiers (iren, firmus, fluidstack, vertiv) carried 2.0-era or misattributed details and were revised in this session; the remaining 27 held.

6. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the Zhou litigation is a reputational rather than financial exposure. Both matters are in San Francisco Superior Court (not the Northern District, as one earlier dossier text implied); the court compelled arbitration on 20 July 2026 and stayed the case, so nothing further will surface publicly unless an award is confirmed. The allegation that matters to clients — that MNPI from a Patel investment vehicle was pushed into paid models — is unproven and denied, but KuCoin reported in April 2026 that clients had 'begun questioning the firm's confidential data handling practices'. We have no evidence of client loss.

7. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the datacenter-power research line is the firm's bridge into this corpus's grid and power-conversion coverage, and that its forecasts should be read as scenario framing: the 800 VDC series (Part 1, 26 May 2026) gave the four-phase transition and the SST market figure (~USD 32bn by 2030 at '$1.25M/MW') that the vertiv dossier now attributes correctly; the behind-the-meter series put US BTM datacentre capacity 'towards 40GW+' by 2028; the PJM post (16 August 2026) argued a USD 12bn modelling error. These are analyst estimates with stated assumptions, not forecasts the firm is accountable for, and the firm sells the Energy and Industrials Models that underlie them.

COLLECTION GAPS — (a) no client list: whether any rated provider buys models, assessments or consulting is unknown; (b) no paid-subscriber count, revenue actuals or margin — only The Information's ~USD 20m (2025) and the >USD 100m 2026 projection; (c) no badge-licence terms — clustermax.ai invites 'licensing inquiries' but publishes no fee or policy; (d) Fund I's actual close — USD 400m filed versus USD 500m company-confirmed, with no amount sold on EDGAR at 2026-10-04; (e) the arbitration's outcome, which is private; (f) the full list of SemiAnalysis Capital and Patel personal holdings against the ClusterMAX roster — only Fluidstack (SPV), Positron, Thinking Machines Lab, Enfabrica and Prime Intellect are reported; (g) no first-party photograph or biography of any leader is published.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — a Form D/A for SemiAnalysis Capital Fund I, LP showing an amount sold (confirms the USD 400m or USD 500m close and dates the fund's investing period); a ClusterMAX 3.1 or 4.0 edition that restores a compensation or holdings disclosure (tests Judgments 2 and 4) or that re-rates Fluidstack, Nscale or HUMAIN from 'Unavailable'; the first rated provider to dispute a tier publicly (none has — Cirrascale sent 'a legal letter' over a description, per the 3.0 text); a confirmed arbitration award or settlement in the Zhou matter; a published client or holdings list; InferenceX hardware provenance moving from provider-donated to independently procured compute; and the cadence promise — 3.0 says ratings refresh roughly every six months, so a 4.0 around March 2027 is the test of whether the system is maintained.
